A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multilingual hallucination study. Their complete text, tables, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the revised title and pagination.

before.justification: V3 reports original detector evaluations, human annotation results, hallucination-rate estimates for 11 LLMs across 30 languages, and an appendix manual analysis.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds a mixed-effects analysis of factors associated with hallucination rates.

M1.justification: The translated-data training pipeline, Llama-3-8B detector, bidirectional/causal variants, QLoRA training and precision/recall-adjusted hallucination estimator are unchanged. The new regression analyzes results without modifying the proposed detector or estimator.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 30-language coverage, five gold-annotated languages, FAVA-derived detection data and 51,133-query LFQA corpus. Section 4.3 adds analysis of retained experimental factors without introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains MONO Bidirect, MULTI Bidirect and MULTI Causal for the same comparisons. The hallucination-rate comparisons also retain the same 11 LLMs from six families.

E3.justification: New Section 4.3 introduces a linear mixed-effects analysis with hallucination rate as outcome, model-size groups of 1.7–3B versus 7–9B, language support, response length and all two-way interactions. Existing training, data splits and generation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds a joint analysis testing dependencies among model size, language support and response length, extending v3's separate comparisons and correlations. Existing silver/gold validation, response-length analyses and Appendix A.7 manual inspection are retained.

E5.justification: V4 first marks selected Table 3 scores as significantly higher at p<0.05 and adds likelihood-ratio and interaction significance reporting in Section 4.3. The existing three detector runs, five generation seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Existing F1 scores and hallucination-rate results are retained, but Table 3 adds significance declarations. Section 4.3 newly reports a likelihood-ratio statistic of 22.14 (p<0.001), a size-by-language-support coefficient of 1.33 (p<0.001), and a size-by-response-length coefficient of -1.02 (p=0.001).

T1.justification: Equation 1 and the precision/recall derivation in Appendix A.4, Equations 2–7, are unchanged. The hallucination taxonomy and informativeness definitions are also retained; the new statistical analysis introduces no formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds the claim that model size moderates language-support and response-length effects, with smaller models suffering disproportionately. The original detector, dataset and multilingual LFQA estimation contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets scaling as providing compound benefits and robustness to multilingual support and longer responses. The longer-response interpretation conflicts with Figure 6b. The limitations also add that resources for assessing multilingual factual coverage are lacking.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 revises the evaluation-data statement from 'We will release' to 'We release.' This updates the documented release statement, although both versions already provide the same repository link. Training details, hardware, generation settings and prompts are unchanged; newly accessible resources cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work section are unchanged. Citations added at the end of Section 3.2 point to Li et al. (2023b) and Dukić and Šnajder (2024), already discussed for decoder-to-encoder adaptation, without introducing new literature or substantively changing research positioning.

P1.justification: The title and several passages replace 'in the wild' with 'realistic' settings. V4 inserts Section 4.3, extends the conclusion, completes the unfinished limitations sentence and updates acknowledgments. Most prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds the two-panel interaction plot in Figure 6, adds significance markers and a legend to Table 3, and edits Figure 1's caption. Existing displays are retained, with subsequent figures renumbered and nearby text and tables reflowed.

improvement.justification: The added interaction analysis and significance reporting could strengthen the paper, but its principal new interpretation is internally inconsistent. Figure 6b shows the small-model line falling below the large-model line for longer responses, whereas Section 4.3 and the conclusion claim a larger-model advantage. The random-effects structure is also unspecified. With the established experiments unchanged, these unresolved problems in the main addition prevent a reliable assessment of the net quality change.
